newsitem.title: UK: N.SEA CRUDE WEAKER, INACTIVE ON IRAQ GREEN LIGHT.
newsitem.headline: N.SEA CRUDE WEAKER, INACTIVE ON IRAQ GREEN LIGHT.

text.p: North Sea crudes weakened on Friday but business was inactive with buyers stubbornly cautious ahead of a resumption of Iraqi exports, traders said.
Business on both physical and cash markets was slow as buyers hung back in hopes of more aggressive offers.
A cargo of Brent loading August 20-22 that was sold at September -20 cents on Thursday was re-offered by the buyer at the same differential on Friday, traders said.
A European major also offered a Brent loading August 17-19 at September -20 cents. Offers came from five to 10 cents below that level but neither party budged.

One holder of several Brents said he felt news that the United Nations had given Iraq the green light to sell oil again for the first time since May was not sufficient grounds for lowering his asking price further towards the bid.

But he acknowledge values could well take a pummeling from Monday onwards when the date for the first lifting of Iraqi oil could become apparent. Traders said the first oil could move as early as midweek.
"Clearly the front of the market will get weaker," said a crude trader, commenting on the expected revival next week of Iraqi crude exports.
"Refiners are holding off and holding off, waiting for the lower numbers."
Outright prices sagged on news that the U.N. Sanctions Committee had approved pricing formulas submitted by Iraq for the fresh exports of Kirkuk and Basrah Light grades.
Front month September IPE crude futures were trading at $18.55 a barrel, down 35 cents.
The cash market was also softer. September Brent outright traded at $18.90 and $18.82, a dollar under Wednesday's traded level.
Intermonths were weaker, with Sep/October done at -17 cents. Oct/Nov was talked at -16/-11 cents.
Brent Contracts for Difference eased around two cents across the board, with next week at September -20/-18 cents and the week after at October -36/-32.

Business in Mediterranean and West African grades was idle with traders seemingly paralysed by the advent of Iraqi barrels. Urals was notionally steady at Dated -95 cents. Bonny was steady at around 40 cents over Dated.
In other developments Mobil Corp said it had issued letters of force majeure to lifters of Nigerian Oso informing them of delays to loadings because of a longer than expected shutdown.
A Mobil spokesman added the company hoped to restart production on Saturday morning. A technical failure prompted a shutdown of the 100,000 barrels per day condensate field early last week.
